chunks: And from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) who said: 'Allah has made forbearance obligatory upon the righteous in His Book.'
It was asked, 'What is forbearance?' He said: 'When your need is less than his need, you request from him (or give to him, leaving the surplus to him).'
And he (peace be upon him) said regarding the words of Allah (Glorified is His Majesty): 'And they prefer others to themselves, even if they themselves are needy.'
He said: 'Do not keep for yourself what he is in greater need of than you are.'

key_terms.التَّمَحُّل: Forbearance, selflessness, or yielding place to others; literally 'making room'.
key_terms.الْأَبْرَار: The righteous, those who are pious and good.
key_terms.تَسْتَأْثِرْ: You monopolize or keep for yourself exclusively.
key_terms.يُؤْثِرُونَ: They prefer or give preference to others.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic definition of Tamahhul and how does it relate to prioritizing others' needs?
ai.summary: In *Kitab al-Mumin*, Imam Ali (a.s.) defines *al-tamahhul* as the active prioritization of a believer's needs over one's own, even when one is also in need, illustrating the practical application of selflessness. This concept is rooted in the Quranic verse 59:9 regarding the Ansar, instructing believers not to hoard resources that their brother in faith needs more than they do. This hadith serves as a foundational ethical guideline in Shia jurisprudence for social solidarity and the rights of the believer over the believer.
